rule: good. the habitual convening, the Council as the one convening, and the full-moon time slot are all carried, and nothing beyond the words is asserted.
texts: good. the condition and the convening come out as one rule the reasoner can fire, with each convening tied to the full moon it happens under and the Watch kept as its place.
good. a fireable rule whose condition is the plain fact that the moon is full, so a later statement that the moon is full can trigger it.

mixed: 'rarely' does get through as a weak claim, but 'at other times' becomes an invented time symbol that names no actual occasion, so a reader cannot tell which times are meant, and the quantifier record is filed against councils in general although the sentence is about this one Council. Recast it as a proportion over the meetings themselves, which needs no name for the excluded times: "Most of the Council's meetings happen at full moon."
